- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.27), especially in early forecast periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.11) over recent days — model tends to ignore downward momentum.
- Overshoot in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon after a sharp price spike — model reacts too quickly to recent highs.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the middle of forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Lagged correction: if sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model fails to adjust forecast downward in time — delay in recognizing sentiment reversal.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days if sentiment is positive, then corrects later — model overweights early sentiment.
- Avoid averaging sentiment over 18 days — sentiment volatility matters more than mean; model should respond to recent sentiment swings, not lagging averages.
